events.title: Yale study reveals prescription drugs and exercise slow aging; supplements ineffective

takeaways: Analyzed 51 studies on anti-aging interventions
Measured using DNA-based blood tests for biological aging
Prescription drugs, healthy diet, and exercise showed measurable effects
Popular over-the-counter anti-aging supplements largely ineffective
Changes in biological age markers do not necessarily mean longer lifespan or disease avoidance

events.title: FBI warns of Artex tool automating cyberattacks at machine speed
events.one_liner: The FBI warned November 13 of Artex, an open-source AI platform released in August 2026 that chains attack techniques to enable breaches from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours. Threat actors with minimal expertise can conduct complex multi-target operations simultaneously. The tool proliferates through forks and archived copies despite creator removal; Censys identified over 1,600 publicly exposed instances.
takeaways: Released August 2026 by Chinese engineer Li Puhua on GitHub; creator denied responsibility and removed repo
Enables intrusions from targeting to privileged access in under three hours
Over 1,600 publicly exposed Artex console instances identified; total deployments much higher
Integrates multiple AI models including Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, Kimi; Chinese models most prevalent
Targeted financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductor, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications, legal sectors

events.title: SCKit malware abuses ScreenConnect remote access software

The worm establishes persistence and deploys RelayTrap to target IT technician workstations, enabling attackers to distribute payloads across managed networks.
takeaways: Attack began November 11, 2026 targeting MSP cloud-hosted ScreenConnect instances
SCKit worm uses scheduled tasks and registry Run entries for persistence
RelayTrap component targets IT support technician workstations via authenticated ScreenConnect sessions
Attackers issue commands through compromised ScreenConnect to silently install unauthorized remote-access clients
Enables remote administration and further tool deployment across victim's managed endpoints

events.title: Prescribed Fire Reduces Giant Sequoia Mortality by Over 50% During Wildfire
events.one_liner: A new study from the University of Nevada, Reno found that prescribed fire treatments in California's Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest cut giant sequoia tree mortality by more than half during the 2020 Castle Fire. This demonstrates that reintroducing fire—a natural ecological process suppressed for nearly 200 years—can restore resilience in these ancient trees and protect them from increasingly severe wildfires.
takeaways: Prescribed fire reduced giant sequoia mortality by more than 50% during the 2020 Castle Fire at Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest
Study conducted at the world's largest giant sequoia grove in the southern Sierra Nevada
Nearly 200 years of fire suppression and absence of Indigenous burning practices have left giant sequoias vulnerable to unprecedented mortality rates
Research published by University of Nevada, Reno College of Agriculture, Biotechnology & Natural Resources
